grades.quote: subdivide the 20-bit page number into its left-hand 10 bits (the page directory index) and its right-hand 10 bits (the page table index).
grades.reason: Describes the IA-32 two-level page table walk step by step. It covers splitting the virtual address into a page directory index, a page table index and an offset. It also covers locating the page directory through a special register, loading the directory entry, checking its valid bit, and using its pointer to reach the page table chunk. This directly answers how a virtual address is translated through multiple page-table levels.
